result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers cover the same core moves: cutting the stagger, tab slide and bounce; adding save and lab-result feedback; toning down the shake; and keeping the refill checkmark. B wins because it adds an explicit order of attack (cheap cuts first, save feedback as the best-value addition, lab results started early) and doesn't make A's unsupported claim that 'your users skew older.' B is a little longer and more spec-heavy, but the extra detail (interruptible tabs, the WCAG three-flash concern, keeping opacity under reduced motion) earns its place. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers cover the same ground well: cutting the stagger, the tab slide and the logo bounce, adding save and lab-result feedback, keeping the refill checkmark, and softening the error shake with text. A wins because it gives an explicit order of attack (ship the cuts first, start the lab-results work early) and ties the cuts to repeated use, such as tabs being the most frequent interaction. B asserts that 'your users skew older' with nothing to support it, which is unsupported usage data.
